description:
Residual from bedrock-w10's cold review (the Director now reads the bootstrap from object storage at recovery start).

The w10 fix covers clusters whose nodes share one object store. Two real configurations still hand a new leader's Director a nil prior core state, which routes recovery to InitializationPhase and re-initializes a live cluster (the w10 wipe):

1. No object storage resolvable on the leader (e.g. a coordination-only node with no nested :path and no top-level object_storage): PersistencePhase never writes a bootstrap, and the only prior state is what the leader's own Directors notified its coordinator. A follower that wins leadership has nothing.
2. Multi-node clusters that fall back to per-node LocalFilesystem (derived from each node's :path): each leader writes its own disk; a new leader's read returns :not_found, which reads as "fresh".

FDB has no such mode: the coordinators' DBCoreState is the quorum-replicated durable record every recovery reads. Expected: a multi-node cluster must either have a shared durable core-state record or refuse to run without one — never treat "I can't see a record" as "fresh cluster" when other coordinators exist. Related: bedrock-1cp (single object-storage resolution; its residual notes nothing flags a multi-node cluster on per-node local storage).
title: Clusters without a shared object store have no durable core state: a follower that wins leadership still recovers from nil
